final.executive_summary: Underweight AAPL: rebalance to a 0.25% target weight of total equity (~$249, ~0.79 shares), trimming about 0.81 of our 1.6036 shares at the next session open (full exit of the residual on a close below 309.10–309.32, per the research's downside trigger). Add nothing anywhere between 309.30 and 317.04; the only technically clean long trigger (>317.04 close on >50M shares, confirmed above 320.28) is 0.78% above spot and would require a fresh risk budget rather than an automatic re-add, because 8/19 already showed what a >50M-share upside attempt at 319.28 does (rejected to 311.30, then 309.35). The reason to trim is not a view that Apple's business is impaired — it is a refusal to underwrite ~34.3x a best-case annualized EPS into a binary 9 Sept event with the buyback bid cut, MACD below zero, and an invalidation level inside the research's own noise band. Horizon 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the 9 Sept event and the late-October FQ4 FY26 print.
final.investment_thesis:
The three seats converge on the action and disagree only on whether to stop at 0.25% or go to zero, so the rating turns on which side wins the substance of the AAPL view, not on the ~$250 of notional. The bear wins the substance; the bull wins the argument against full liquidation; the neutral wins the sizing.

What the bear proved, on dated evidence: (1) Earnings quality. Opex +22.9% outpaced revenue +16.4%, so the entire 152-bp nine-month operating-margin expansion came from gross margin — and roughly two-thirds of operating income growth therefore rests on the same line item exposed to a 94% inventory build with raw materials +260%. A 20% write-down on incremental raw materials is ~100 bps of quarterly gross margin against the 357 bps being underwritten. The bull cannot treat that build as a launch pre-build and simultaneously dismiss it as a margin risk; it is one datapoint. (2) Cash-flow quality. The +52.5% nine-month FCF leans on ~$47B of favorable working-capital swings, a 21% AR decline that cannot recur, and a 28% capex reduction that is a deferral; the durable figure is net income +20.0%, so the $9.17 defended at 34.3x is a best-case quarter annualized with no forward guidance anywhere in the packet. (3) The premium's mechanism has been removed: buybacks cut to 67% of FCF from 113.6%, share count down only 1.11% over nine months while SBC grew 7.4% — the multiple is retained, the EPS turbo is not. (4) The forward indicator points the wrong way: current deferred revenue +5.3% against +16% revenue growth. (5) The tape offers no asymmetry: the bull's 311.50 invalidation sits 0.43x ATR from spot, with the 10-EMA and 50-SMA fused 0.0003 apart at that level — a coin flip that guarantees a noise stop-out without the thesis being falsified — while the downside trigger at 309.10–309.32 needs no volume confirmation and the 317.04 upside trigger needs >50M shares against a 34.8M five-day average. Two rejections at 317–320, with the strongest up-volume session since the crash (8/19, +2.19% on 50.5M shares) topping and closing lower, is distribution, not base-building, and MACD at -0.733 is repair, not resumption. Price sits 0.78% below the upper band of a 4.99% squeeze two weeks before a binary event the news review itself calls sell-the-news-prone.

What the bull proved, and why this is neither a Sell with a zero target nor a Hold: nothing reported has broken. Revenue +16.4% to $109.4B, gross margin 50.06% (+357 bps), EPS +28.7%, net cash ~$62.2B up 84%, current ratio above 1.0 for the first time, and price 11.4% above a rising 200-SMA at 282.35 with the 50-SMA 9.36% above it and VWMA reclaimed at 309.10. That structure argues against an earnings-collapse short, and it is why the position is trimmed rather than liquidated. I also accept the bull's point that the '35x / perfection priced in' framing traces to an unsourced opinion piece — but opinion pieces on both sides cancel, and the 34.3x arithmetic on the supplied $9.17 is not an opinion.

Where I overrule the seats. The conservative's push to zero is rejected: it is a defensible tie, not a superior risk decision, and the difference between $249 and $0 of exposure on a $99,604 account is economically negligible — while the conservative's own framing (certain zero vs uncertain negative) misapplies a solvency argument to a rounding error, and its supporting observation that the 50/200 spread has compressed from 31.54 to 29.17 is a reason to watch, not a reason to liquidate a stub. The aggressive's plan to re-enter with 'actual size' above 317.04/320.28 is rejected on the conservative's continuity critique and the neutral's 8/19 precedent: that entry is at the top of the range, in the wake of a squeeze resolution, thirteen days before a binary event, executed at an unknown next-session open — the same continuity assumption he attacks on the stop side. The neutral wins the sizing with the one correction that matters: 309.10 is a review-and-exit trigger, not an executable stop, and 317.04/320.28 are confirmation levels requiring a fresh risk budget, not orders.

What would change the rating. Upgrade toward Overweight and rebuild toward 1.0–1.5% on: (1) a daily close above 317.04 on >50M shares followed by a close above 320.28, breaking the two-rejection pattern; (2) MACD reclaiming zero (roughly +0.73 from -0.733) with RSI above 60; (3) FQ4 FY26 gross margin at or above 49.5% with the $13.3B intangible credibly explained as value-accretive rather than a deferred obligation against the matched $13.5B liability; (4) current deferred revenue re-accelerating toward the revenue growth rate; (5) evidence the 9 Sept event delivers an ASP step-function rather than a spec bump. Downgrade to Sell / exit the stub entirely on a daily close below 309.10–309.32, or below 300.57 to break the four-test 300 shelf — noting the 300.37 hard stop sits only 0.37 above the crash low, so effective slippage in a name that just printed a -10% intraday gap is 7–8%, not 4.5%.

Risks to this call, stated plainly: if 9 Sept lands a genuine foldable/ASP step-function and FQ4 holds gross margin above 49.5% with inventory converting, the multiple is defensible on the accelerating base and this trim will have sold into strength — and with the re-entry gate only 0.78% above spot, the five-day mark is likely to look premature even if the thesis holds. Data gaps, not papered over: no forward guidance or consensus EPS in the packet, no segment/geographic mix, no options or implied-vol data, no resolved intangibles footnote, and the news sample is partial — so every level here is technical and quality-of-earnings based, not a full valuation. Cost basis of $314.85 and the -$405.69 realized P&L are irrelevant to this decision.
